Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. All three services were restarted, and every piece of state survived.

## What I restarted

| # | Service | Restart mechanism | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cloud SQL Postgres `umami-pgdb-01` | `gcloud sql instances restart` — a real cold restart of the database engine | back to `RUNNABLE` |
| 2 | Cloud Run `umami-acs521ba68a` | new revision → all container instances replaced and old ones drained | `umami-acs521ba68a-00001-qcm` → **`-00002-rc4`** |
| 3 | Cloud Run `alcove` | same | `alcove-00002-pfw` → **`-00003-s5s`** |

Cloud Run has no "restart" verb; rolling to a new revision *is* the platform's restart — the previously running containers are terminated and replaced with fresh ones.

## Storage was already durable, and I hardened it further
Nothing was ephemeral to begin with: umami's users, websites, sessions and pageview events all live in the Cloud SQL Postgres instance on persistent disk, and both Cloud Run containers are stateless (alcove's HTML is baked into its image; `APP_SECRET` is a service-level env var, so it survives revision changes and keeps existing sessions valid).

The one real gap was that I originally created the database with `--no-backup`. I fixed that before restarting: **automated daily backups (7 retained) and point-in-time recovery (3 days of transaction logs)** are now enabled, so the data survives more than just a restart.
